o: Entonces Pablo, habiendo ya mucho que no comíamos, puesto en pie en medio de ellos, dijo: Fuera de cierto conveniente, oh varones, haberme oído, y no partir de Creta, y evitar este inconveniente y daño.
t: Then Paul, since we had long been without food, stood up in the midst of them and said: Men, you ought to have listened to me and not to have departed from Crete, sparing yourselves this inconvenience and damage.

o: Mas ahora os amonesto que tengáis buen ánimo; porque ninguna pérdida habrá de persona de vosotros, sino solamente de la nave.
t: But now I exhort you to be of good courage, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.

o: Porque esta noche ha estado conmigo el ángel del Dios del cual yo soy, y al cual sirvo,
t: For last night the angel of God, whose I am and whom I serve, stood with me,

o: Diciendo: Pablo, no temas; es menester que seas presentado delante de César; y he aquí, Dios te ha dado todos los que navegan contigo.
t: saying, 'Paul, do not be afraid; you must be brought before Caesar; and behold, God has given you all those who are sailing with you.'

o: Por tanto, oh varones, tened buen ánimo; porque yo confío en Dios que será así como me ha dicho;
t: Therefore, men, be of good courage, for I trust in God that it will be just as He has said to me;

o: Si bien es menester que demos en una isla.
t: though it is necessary that we should come ashore on some island.

o: Y venida la décimacuarta noche, y siendo llevados por el mar Adriático, los marineros a la media noche sospecharon que estaban cerca de alguna tierra;
t: And when the fourteenth night had come, as we were being driven through the Adriatic Sea, the sailors suspected that we were approaching some land;

o: Y echando la sonda, hallaron veinte brazas; y pasando un poco más adelante, volviendo a echar la sonda, hallaron quince brazas.
t: and taking soundings, they found twenty fathoms; and passing a little farther on and taking soundings again, they found fifteen fathoms.

o: Y habiendo temor de dar en lugares escabrosos, echando cuatro anclas de la popa, deseaban que se hiciese de día.
t: And fearing that we might run aground on rocky places, they dropped four anchors from the stern and wished for day to break.

o: Entonces procurando los marineros huir de la nave, echado que hubieron el esquife a la mar, aparentando como que querían largar las anclas de proa,
t: Then the sailors, seeking to escape from the ship, had already lowered the small boat into the sea, pretending that they wanted to let go the anchors from the bow,

o: Pablo dijo al centurión y a los soldados: Si éstos no quedan en la nave, vosotros no podéis salvaros.
t: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers: If these men do not remain in the ship, you cannot be saved.

o: Entonces los soldados cortaron los cabos del esquife, y dejáronlo perder.
t: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the small boat and let it drift away.

o: Y como comenzó a ser de día, Pablo exhortaba a todos que comiesen, diciendo: Este es el décimocuarto día que esperáis y permanecéis ayunos, no comiendo nada.
t: And as day began to dawn, Paul urged everyone to eat, saying: This is the fourteenth day you have been waiting and continuing to fast, eating nothing.

o: Por tanto, os ruego que comáis por vuestra salud: que ni aun un cabello de la cabeza de ninguno de vosotros perecerá.
t: Therefore, I urge you to eat for your own survival, for not even a hair of the head of any of you will perish.

o: Y habiendo dicho esto, tomando el pan, hizo gracias a Dios en presencia de todos, y partiendo, comenzó a comer.
t: And when he had said this, he took bread, gave thanks to God in the presence of all, and broke it and began to eat.

o: Entonces todos teniendo ya mejor ánimo, comieron ellos también.
t: Then all, being now of better heart, also ate.

o: Y éramos todas las personas en la nave doscientas setenta y seis.
t: And we were altogether two hundred and seventy-six persons in the ship.

o: Y satisfechos de comida, aliviaban la nave, echando el grano a la mar.
t: And having been satisfied with food, they lightened the ship, throwing the grain overboard into the sea.

o: Y como se hizo de día, no conocían la tierra: mas veían un golfo que tenía orilla, al cual acordaron echar, si pudiesen, la nave.
t: And when it was day, they did not recognize the land; but they saw a bay with a shore, and they agreed, if they could, to run the ship into it.

o: Cortando pues las anclas, las dejaron en la mar, largando también las ataduras de los gobernalles; y alzada la vela mayor al viento, íbanse a la orilla.
t: So, cutting off the anchors, they left them in the sea, and also letting go the lashings of the rudders; and raising the mainsail to the wind, they made for the shore.

o: Mas dando en un lugar de dos aguas, hicieron encallar la nave; y la proa, hincada, estaba sin moverse, y la popa se abría con la fuerza de la mar.
t: But having run aground in a place where two currents met, the ship ran aground; and the bow, being stuck fast, did not move, while the stern was being broken up by the force of the sea.

o: Entonces el acuerdo de los soldados era que matasen los presos, porque ninguno se fugase nadando.
t: Then the soldiers' plan was to kill the prisoners, so that none might escape by swimming.

o: Mas el centurión, queriendo salvar a Pablo, estorbó este acuerdo, y mandó que los que pudiesen nadar, se echasen los primeros, y saliesen a tierra;
t: But the centurion, wishing to save Paul, prevented that plan and commanded those who could swim to go first and get out to land;

o: Y los demás, parte en tablas, parte en cosas de la nave. Y así aconteció que todos se salvaron saliendo a tierra.
t: and the rest, some on planks, some on pieces of the ship. And so it came about that everyone was saved by getting out onto the land.

o: Y CUANDO escapamos, entonces supimos que la isla se llamaba Melita.
t: And when we had escaped, then we knew that the island was called Melita.

o: Y los bárbaros nos mostraron no poca humanidad; porque, encendido un fuego, nos recibieron a todos, a causa de la lluvia que venía, y del frío.
t: And the barbarians showed us no little kindness; for they lit a fire and welcomed us all, because of the rain that was coming and the cold.

o: Entonces habiendo Pablo recogido algunos sarmientos, y puéstolos en el fuego, una víbora, huyendo del calor, le acometió a la mano.
t: Then when Paul had gathered up some brushwood and laid it on the fire, a viper, fleeing from the heat, fastened on his hand.

o: Y como los bárbaros vieron la víbora colgando de su mano, decían los unos a los otros: Ciertamente este hombre es homicida, a quien, escapado de la mar, la justicia no deja vivir.
t: And when the barbarians saw the viper hanging from his hand, they said to one another: Surely this man is a murderer, who, though he escaped the sea, justice does not allow to live.

o: Mas él, sacudiendo la víbora en el fuego, ningún mal padeció.
t: But he, shaking off the viper into the fire, suffered no harm.

o: Empero ellos estaban esperando cuándo se había de hinchar, o caer muerto de repente; mas habiendo esperado mucho, y viendo que ningún mal le venía, mudados, decían que era un dios.
t: Yet they kept waiting to see whether he would swell up or fall dead suddenly; but after waiting a long time and seeing that no harm came to him, they changed their minds and said that he was a god.

o: En aquellos lugares había heredades del principal de la isla, llamado Publio, el cual nos recibió y hospedó tres días humanamente.
t: Now in those places there were estates of the chief man of the island, whose name was Publius, who received us and lodged us three days courteously.

o: Y aconteció que el padre de Publio estaba en cama, enfermo de fiebres y de disentería: al cual Pablo entró, y después de haber orado, le puso las manos encima, y le sanó:
t: And it happened that the father of Publius was lying in bed, sick of fevers and dysentery; and Paul went in to him, and after praying, laid his hands on him and healed him:

o: Y esto hecho, también los otros que en la isla tenían enfermedades, llegaban, y eran sanados:
t: And so it was also that the others who had diseases on the island came, and were healed:

o: Los cuales también nos honraron con muchos obsequios; y cuando partimos, nos cargaron de las cosas necesarias.
t: And they also honored us with many gifts; and when we sailed away, they loaded us with the things we needed.

o: Así que, pasados tres meses, navegamos en una nave Alejandrina que había invernado en la isla, la cual tenía por enseña a Cástor y Pólux.
t: So, after three months, we sailed in an Alexandrian ship that had wintered in the island, whose figurehead was the Twin Brothers.

o: Y llegados a Siracusa, estuvimos allí tres días.
t: And when we had come to Syracuse, we stayed there three days.

o: De allí, costeando alrededor, vinimos a Regio; y otro día después, soplando el austro, vinimos al segundo día a Puteolos:
t: From there, coasting around, we came to Rhegium; and the next day, with the south wind blowing, we came on the second day to Puteoli:

o: Donde habiendo hallado hermanos, nos rogaron que quedásemos con ellos siete días; y luego vinimos a Roma;
t: Where, having found brothers, they urged us to stay with them seven days; and so we came to Rome;

o: De donde, oyendo de nosotros los hermanos, nos salieron a recibir hasta la plaza de Appio, y Las Tres Tabernas: a los cuales como Pablo vio, dio gracias a Dios, y tomó aliento.
t: And from there, when the brothers heard of us, they came to meet us as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns; and when Paul saw them, he gave thanks to God and took courage.

o: Y como llegamos a Roma, el centurión entregó los presos al prefecto de los ejércitos, mas a Pablo fue permitido estar por sí, con un soldado que le guardase.
t: And when we arrived at Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard, but Paul was permitted to live by himself with a soldier who guarded him.

o: Y aconteció que tres días después, Pablo convocó a los principales de los Judíos; a los cuales, luego que estuvieron juntos, les dijo: Yo, varones hermanos, no habiendo hecho nada contra el pueblo, ni contra los ritos de la patria, he sido entregado preso desde Jerusalem en manos de los Romanos;
t: And it happened that three days later, Paul summoned the leading men of the Jews; and when they had gathered together, he said to them: Men and brothers, having done nothing against the people or against the customs of our country, I was handed over as a prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.

o: Los cuales, habiéndome examinado, me querían soltar, por no haber en mí ninguna causa de muerte.
t: And when they had examined me, they wanted to set me free, because there was no cause of death in me.

o: Mas contradiciendo los Judíos, fui forzado a apelar a César; no que tenga de qué acusar a mi nación.
t: But when the Jews opposed me, I was forced to appeal to Caesar; not because I had anything to accuse my nation of.

o: Así que, por esta causa, os he llamado para veros y hablaros; porque por la esperanza de Israel estoy rodeado de esta cadena.
t: Therefore, for this reason I have called you to see you and speak with you, because for the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.

o: Entonces ellos le dijeron: Nosotros ni hemos recibido cartas tocante a ti de Judea, ni ha venido alguno de los hermanos que haya denunciado o hablado algún mal de ti.
t: Then they said to him: We have received no letter concerning you from Judea, nor has any brother come who has reported or spoken any evil of you.

o: Mas querríamos oir de ti lo que sientes; porque de esta secta notorio nos es que en todos lugares es contradicha.
t: But we would like to hear from you what you think; for concerning this sect, it is well known to us that it is spoken against everywhere.

o: Y habiéndole señalado un día, vinieron a él muchos a la posada, a los cuales declaraba y testificaba el reino de Dios, persuadiéndoles lo concerniente a Jesús, por la ley de Moisés y por los profetas, desde la mañana hasta la tarde.
t: And when they had set him a day, many came to him at his lodging, to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both by the law of Moses and by the prophets, from morning until evening.

o: Y algunos asentían a lo que se decía, mas algunos no creían.
t: And some consented to what was said, but some did not believe.

o: Y como fueron entre sí discordes, se fueron, diciendo Pablo esta palabra: Bien ha hablado el Espíritu Santo por el profeta Isaías a nuestros padres,
t: And when they disagreed among themselves, they departed, Paul saying this word: The Holy Spirit spoke rightly by the prophet Isaiah to our fathers,

o: Diciendo: Ve a este pueblo, y di les: De oído oiréis, y no entenderéis; y viendo veréis, y no percibiréis:
t: Saying, "Go to this people and tell them: By hearing you will hear, but you will not understand; and seeing you will see, but you will not perceive."

o: Porque el corazón de este pueblo se ha engrosado, y de los oídos oyeron pesadamente, y sus ojos taparon; porque no vean con los ojos, y oigan con los oídos, y entiendan de corazón, y se conviertan, y yo los sane.
t: For the heart of this people has become callous, and their ears have been dull of hearing, and their eyes have been closed; so they do not see with their eyes, nor hear with their ears, nor understand with their heart, nor turn and be healed.

o: Séaos pues notorio que a los Gentiles es enviada esta salud de Dios: y ellos oirán.
t: Be it known to you then, that this salvation of God has been sent to the Gentiles; and they will hear it.

o: Y habiendo dicho esto, los Judíos salieron, teniendo entre sí gran contienda.
t: And after he had said this, the Jews went out, having great strife among themselves.

o: Pablo empero, quedó dos años enteros en su casa de alquiler, y recibía a todos los que a él venían,
t: Paul, however, remained for two full years in his rented house, and welcomed all who came to him,

o: Predicando el reino de Dios y enseñando lo que es del Señor Jesucristo con toda libertad, sin impedimento.
t: proclaiming the kingdom of God and teaching what is concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness, without hindrance.
